chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked

about two men who had a slave between them, and one of them emancipated his share. So he said: If it was harmful, he would be obligated to emancipate the whole of him; otherwise, the slave would work to (earn the value of) the other half.

key_terms.اسْتُسْعِيَ: shall work/be put to work — from سَعَى (to strive/work); a technical legal term for the slave being permitted to earn money through labor to purchase his own remaining share of freedom
key_terms.عَبْدٌ: slave — a person held in bondage as property under classical Islamic law
key_terms.كُلِّفَ: was obligated/assigned — the legal obligation imposed on the partner who caused the partial emancipation
key_terms.مُضَارّاً: causing harm — the criterion triggering the obligation to fully emancipate; juridically ambiguous but generally refers to leaving the slave in an uncertain legal status
key_terms.نَصِيبَهُ: his share — referring to the co-owner's portion (typically one-half) of the jointly-owned slave

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on a jointly-owned slave when one partner emancipates his share?
ai.summary: This hadith presents Imam al-Sadiq's ruling on the legal case of a jointly-owned slave when one co-owner emancipates his share. The ruling distinguishes two scenarios: if the partial emancipation causes harm to the slave (such as leaving him in an ambiguous legal status), the emancipating co-owner must buy out the other's share and free the slave entirely. If no harm results, the slave himself may work to earn his freedom for the remaining half. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle that individual rights are balanced against broader harm, and demonstrates the Imam's role as a legal authority in resolving novel cases brought by his companions.
word_analysis: the slave shall work (to earn his freedom)

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, form his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from hammad, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having been asked

about two men what had a slave between the two of them, so one of the two emancipated his share. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If it was harmful, he would be assigned to emancipate the whole of him, or else the slave would have to work regarding the other half’.
